chunks: And from a letter of his (peace be upon him) to 'Umar ibn Abi Salamah al-Makhzumi, who was his governor over Bahrain; so he dismissed him and appointed an-Nu'man ibn 'Ajlan al-Zurqi in his place.

key_terms.الْزُرْقِيَّ: Al-Zurqi (the one with blue eyes/skin, a nisba)

ai.seo_question: Who replaced Umar ibn Abi Salamah as governor of Bahrain according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This episode from Nahj al-Balagha illustrates Imam Ali’s (AS) dynamic administrative style, demonstrating his willingness to correct inefficiencies or misconduct by replacing 'Umar ibn Abi Salamah with the more capable an-Nu'man ibn 'Ajlan. It underscores the Shia scholarly view of the Imam as not only a spiritual guide but also a pragmatic statesman who prioritized effective governance and accountability in the early Islamic provinces.
